units.passage: AI Use Description AI is used creatively to enhance problem-solving, generate novel ideas, or develop innovative problems. Students and educators co-design assessments to explore unique AI applications within the field of study. Student AI Use Expectation You should use AI creatively to solve the task, potentially co-designing new approaches with your instructor. Associated AI-Resistant Strategies Define and provide access to the OIT permitted AI tool(s) students are permitted to use for the activity/assignment. Work with students to develop an ethics-based use policy. Demonstrate and have students practice using the permitted tools in the way they are being asked to use them. Have students capture their use of the AI tool through screenshots, process steps, and/or a summary. This should include an explanation of how they upheld the ethics-based use policy. units.passage: and the relationship between those sections and student contributions should be discussed in cover letters that accompany the essay submission.
units.why: 'the relationship between those sections and student contributions should be discussed in cover letters' asks for a written reflection on AI use with the submission (P26).

units.passage: Explain what you learned from the AI tool, how you verified its accuracy and reliability, how you integrated its output with your own work, and how you acknowledged its limitations and biases.
units.why: "Explain what you learned from the AI tool, how you verified its accuracy" asks for a reflection on AI use (P26); no transcript is required.
units.fit_note: A written explanation or reflection, not a transcript or log. | Asks for an explanation within the submission rather than keeping transcripts or logs.

units.passage: Provide evidence of how you used the AI tool and how it contributed to your assignment.
units.why: "Provide evidence of how you used the AI tool" requires documentation of use (P26).
units.fit_note: Evidence form is unspecified; need not be a transcript.

units.passage: Use it to complete a small task (e.g., generate code, solve a math problem, draft a lesson plan). Document: » What you asked the AI » What it produced » How you evaluated its accuracy » Any limitations or errors
units.why: The assignment asks students to document 'What you asked the AI' and 'What it produced', a record of prompt and output, so P26.
units.fit_note: Sample assignment component; also asks for how accuracy was evaluated and limitations noted. | Applies to a sample assignment, recording prompt, output and accuracy evaluation.

units.passage: What ethical principles guided your use » How you ensured responsible use (e.g., citation, verification) » Whether you would use it again and under what conditions
units.why: The reflection essay asks students to reflect on 'what ethical principles guided your use' and 'how you ensured responsible use', a required reflection on AI use, so P26.

units.passage: Your final project must also include a one-page, single-spaced reflective memo (see memo format here) that assesses your writing and research process, application of course concepts, and use of digital tools (including AI).
units.why: The sample memo requires 'a one-page, single-spaced reflective memo' on 'use of digital tools (including AI)', a required reflection, so P26.

units.passage: Keep careful record and observational notes about the AI-generated bibliography. » Prompt engineering: ask AI to complete part (or all) of your literature review. Rephrase and refine your prompts several times. Layer prompts to build complexity. Include specific requests about content, word count, context, audience, style/ tone, purpose, and larger significance. Keep careful record and observational notes about your prompts and the effectiveness of the outputs.
units.why: Memo asks students to 'Keep careful record and observational notes about your prompts', P26.

units.passage: Attachments: please include your complete outputs.
units.why: 'Attachments: please include your complete outputs' requires submitting the AI outputs, so P26.

units.passage: A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use throughout the course. By keeping track of your AI use and sharing your experiences, we all gain understanding, identify potential issues in this rapidly changing field, and discover better ways to use the resources for our objectives.
units.why: "A portion of your term grade will evaluate your documentation of AI use" requires keeping a record of AI use and grades it. Nearest type is P26; the grading of it is the extra.
units.fit_note: Part of the grade is based on the documentation, which the type does not mention.

units.passage: Requiring documentation of how AI was used in the completion of assignment, such as prompts, iterative work on outputs, or chatbot conversation transcripts
units.why: "Requiring documentation of how AI was used in the completion of assignment, such as prompts, iterative work on outputs, or chatbot conversation transcripts" is a listed option for instructors designing assignments, asking students to keep and submit logs (P26); before-course, may.

units.passage: A simple statement may often suffice (e.g., “I used AI to summarize my notes”), while in other contexts providing citations or evidence of use such as complete chat logs may be more appropriate. This prompts explicit reflection by students on whether they have used AI appropriately and followed relevant university guidelines.
units.why: "providing citations or evidence of use such as complete chat logs may be more appropriate" names chat logs as evidence of AI use, P26 (rather than P24, which covers the simple statement example in the previous sentence).
units.fit_note: Also allows a one-line statement such as 'I used AI to summarize my notes' instead of logs. / Also gives the simple-statement option ("I used AI to summarize my notes") and says disclosure prompts students to reflect.

units.passage: I also require that you document and reflect on your use to have a record of experience and insights. You will do this in an AI journal, updated weekly.
units.why: The same sample says students must "document and reflect on your use ... in an AI journal, updated weekly", which is keeping and submitting reflections, P26.
units.fit_note: Appears in a sample template, not a binding rule. / Sample statement text.

units.passage: When AI tools are used, students must document how they were used and reflect on their impact on learning.
units.why: Option 3 requires students to "document how they were used and reflect on their impact on learning", i.e. keep and submit documentation and reflections (P26).

units.passage: Therefore if you use any of these systems to support your work where assignments specifically allow it, you will be required to describe the uses and process.
units.why: Sample 4: students 'will be required to describe the uses and process' where assignments allow AI, a description/reflection requirement (P26).

units.passage: invite students to use AI to refactor code or generate tests, paired with a repository log and a reflective memo on what they accepted or rejected and why.
units.why: The example pairs AI use with 'a repository log and a reflective memo': logs and reflections (P26).
units.fit_note: Example for a software studio; also invites AI-generated code (P16).

units.passage: To ensure transparency and maintain academic integrity, it is recommended practice to save all chat transcripts from GenAI tools used for assignments. Be sure to retain the full record, including all prompts, inputs and outputs, should your instructor request it
units.policy: It is recommended practice to save all chat transcripts from GenAI tools used for assignments and retain the full record, including all prompts, inputs and outputs, should your instructor request it.
units.why: "it is recommended practice to save all chat transcripts" is a recommendation, so should (both coders said should) and neutral rather than require (A require, B neutral). B's policy wording is used because the anchor alone omits the conditions on retaining the full record.

units.passage: Faculty may request that students provide prompt logs or tool settings for verification of their work.
units.why: "Faculty may request that students provide prompt logs or tool settings" is a verification step open to faculty, not a stance on AI use (A permit, B neutral). P26.

units.passage: Assignments may require you to reflect on your AI use, critique outputs or compare AI-generated material to scholarly work.
units.why: Assignments may "require you to reflect on your AI use", a reflection requirement, P26.
units.fit_note: Reflection is an assignment component here, not only a record of use.

units.passage: Students may be asked to save the AI chat as a PDF file for verification.
units.why: 'Students may be asked to save the AI chat as a PDF file for verification' lets instructors request chat records, so transcripts (P26).

units.passage: Students must save and submit all prompts or questions posed to the GENAI system.
units.why: 'Students must save and submit all prompts or questions posed' requires keeping and submitting logs (P26).

units.passage: Students must provide a complete record of all responses or outputs generated by the GENAI system, regardless of whether the feedback was ultimately used in the assignment or project.
units.why: 'complete record of all responses or outputs generated... regardless of whether the feedback was ultimately used' requires submitting full output records (P26).
